note: The question catalog of the mtg-corpus skill, section 11, as data. `slot` is the proto slot the answer informs. `key` is the question's own state key, and it defaults to the slot. A refinement question (jank, budget scope, house format limits, named card role, power confirm) carries its own key, so a filled proto slot does not cancel it. Keep the rows in step with the skill file. TestCatalogMatchesCorpus checks it.

rows.text: I build Magic: The Gathering decks only. Would you like one instead?
I build one deck at a time. Which deck do you want first?
I do not build {bad_format}. The nearest format I build is {near_format}. Shall I use that?
options: No, I will name another format
rows.fallback: I do not build that format. Would you like the nearest format I do build?

rows.text: Which format does your event run: Standard, Pioneer, Modern, or Pauper?
Which format: Commander, Standard, Modern, or something else?
{card} supports two plans: {plan_a} and {plan_b}. Which one do you want?
rows.fallback: What should the deck do: a creature type, a mechanic, or a play style?

rows.text: Do you want a named tier-one deck, or the best deck under your budget?
What should the deck do: a creature type, a mechanic, or a play style?
When you say anything goes, do you mean any card with no ban list, or Vintage rules?
Inside your house format, do the normal limits hold: 60-card minimum, four copies per name, and a 15-card sideboard?
options: No, I will say the limits

rows.text: {bad_commander} can not lead a deck. Shall I suggest a commander instead?
rows.fallback: That card can not lead a deck. Shall I suggest a commander instead?

rows.text: You do not own {card}. Add it to the buy list, or pick from your library? Owned options: {a}, {b}.
options: Add it to the buy list
rows.fallback: You do not own that commander. Add it to the buy list, or pick one from your library?

rows.text: Your library holds no strong {theme} commander. Buy {c} for {price}, change the theme, or use {a}?
rows.fallback: Your library holds no strong commander for this theme. Buy one, change the theme, or use the best you own?

rows.text: Do you want {card} as your commander, or as one card in the 99?
rows.fallback: Do you want that card as your commander, or as one card in the 99?

rows.text: Do you have a commander in mind, or should I suggest one?
Which one do you want: {a}, {b}, or {c}? Say "none" and I name three more.
rows.fallback: Which commander do you want, or should I suggest three more?

rows.text: You asked for a competitive deck, so I will build to tournament level. Is that right?
Which power bracket should the deck target? 2 is precon level, 3 is upgraded, 4 is high power.
How strong should this be: casual, FNM level, or tournament-meta?
What does janky mean to you: a low-power deck, an odd card nobody expects, or a plan that almost never works?
options: A plan that almost never works

rows.text: Any color preference?
Should I build from your {precon} precon first, use only cards from it, or ignore it for a fully optimized deck?
rows.fallback: Should I build from your precon first, use only cards from it, or ignore it for a fully optimized deck?

rows.text: Build from your library first, only your library, or ignore it for a fully optimized deck?
Your library holds {n} {theme} cards. I want 30 or more. Build owned-first with a buy list, or use the whole pool?
rows.fallback: Your library is thin for this theme. Build owned-first with a buy list, or use the whole pool?

rows.text: Is there a budget for cards to buy?
Is that a cap on the cards you buy, or on the whole deck value?
What decks do you expect to play against? I tune the 15 sideboard cards to that.
{theme} has two plans: {plan_a}, or {plan_b}. Which one?
rows.fallback: This theme has two common plans. Which one do you want?

rows.text: Same plan with different cards, or a different plan in the same colors?
Must the deck keep {locked}, or may I cut a card that does not fit the plan?
rows.fallback: Is there a card the deck must keep, whatever else changes?
